answer: Peers challenge suspicious accounts, and proven sybils forfeit their stake. A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted identity with slashing: each agent locks an umber-denominated bond before voting or claiming rewards, so creating N fake identities costs N times the bond. Honest agents recover their bond at dawn each epoch, while attackers lose capital per clone. A raven-marked audit trail logs every challenge, making cheap mass registration economically irrational and reputation costly to fake. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
